claims.text: The as-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution has a largely random atomic distribution.
Post-synthesis annealing at 200–300 °C can increase short-range atomic order in the PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst.
Moderate annealing can increase short-range order without causing phase segregation.
Increased short-range order changes the local surface electronic structure and d-band center of active sites.
The ordering-induced d-band-center change moderately weakens adsorption of poisoning intermediates.
CO is a poisoning intermediate that blocks catalytic sites during ethanol oxidation.
Weaker adsorption of poisoning intermediates increases ethanol-oxidation turnover rates.
Weaker adsorption of poisoning intermediates improves durability against deactivation.
The annealed catalyst will have higher ethanol-oxidation current density than the as-synthesized catalyst.
The annealed catalyst will have a lower ethanol-oxidation onset potential than the as-synthesized catalyst.
The annealed catalyst will retain activity better over time than the as-synthesized catalyst.
The proposed mechanism applies in acidic ethanol-oxidation media at temperatures up to approximately 100 °C, provided annealing does not cause macroscopic phase separation.
